newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen opening mixed to lower.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen opening mixed to lower.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open mixed to lower Friday after yesterday's 93-point slide by the Dow Industrials.
Analysts said they did not see major downside momentum at the open but that blue chips had to continue their correction after having been overvalued.

"That's where the aggressive overvaluation, the mania, has taken place. The index funds bought blue chips, which in turn way outpaced the rest of the market," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
The market will also see volatility from today's "double-witching" expirations of U.S. U.S. index and individual options contracts.
"Over the last couple of years, closeout days have seen great volume at the start and close of trading but not in the middle," Wachtel said.
He said that the market's fundamentals remained unchanged.

"Interest rates, inflation, profits and cash flow are all still satisfactory. But an area of the market -- the blue chips -- is out of sync with reality," he said. "This does not indict the other 9,000 stocks."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei average was down 17.17 points, or 0.09 percent, at 19,034.54.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was down 36.0 at 4320.1.
U.S. shares in London were little changed from Wall Street closing levels as European investors remained cautious after the Dow's two-day slide.
The dollar strengthened against the yen in Tokyo and inched lower in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly higher, with the 30-year bond up 7/32 to yield 6.64 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street focuses on Rubbermaid Inc. It quotes William Steele, a household products analyst at Dean Witter, as saying that unless Rubbermaid can show its ability to diversify, especially in foreign markets, and perhaps into nonresin-based products, it no longer deserves the lofty price-earnings ratio of a steady-growth consumer products company.

The New York Times Market Place writes that some investors are asking themselves whether Tandy Corp is finally turning itself around after the company reported fourth quarter earnings Thursday which were stronger than expected.
